newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan aluminium premiums follow Japan's downward.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan aluminium premiums follow Japan's downward.

text.p: Taiwan's aluminium import premiums have eased to between US$70 to US$78 a tonne over LME prices, reflecting a US$3 fall in Japan, local traders said on Monday.
"Taiwan's aluminium premium in recent weeks has traded between $70 to $78 a tonne," following Japan's reduction, one local dealer said. Another dealer put the range at US$70-US$75.
Japan aluminium importers recently fixed fourth quarter premiums with Western producers at around US$62 a tonne over LME cash prices -- a drop of about US$3 over the third quarter.
Japan's import premium is used by Taiwan traders as a benchmark. Taiwan's premiums generally are about US$10 higher than Japan's due to its smaller market size and orders.
Taiwan imported about 480,000 tonnes of gross aluminium 1995, up from 450,000 tonnes in 1994.
